scope.flow: disputeTree deposit then resolveDispute resolution with a fee-on-transfer disputeToken
scope.environment: Solidity protocol with disputeToken, disputeTree, resolveDispute, recoverERC20, Merkle tree publishing

statements.text: A fee-on-transfer token is configured as the disputeToken.
A user calls disputeTree() sending disputeAmount tokens (e.g., 1000 tokens).
The FoT token deducts a transfer fee (e.g., 1% = 10 tokens) on the deposit.
disputeTree() records the full disputeAmount but the contract receives fewer tokens (e.g., 990 of 1000) due to the transfer fee, with no record of the actual received amount.
resolveDispute() attempts to transfer the recorded disputeAmount (1000 tokens) in both branches.
resolveDispute() always reverts with "ERC20: transfer amount exceeds balance" because the contract holds only 990 tokens and the FoT transfer burns a fee first.
disputer remains permanently set to the original non-zero address since resolveDispute() is the only function that clears it and it always reverts.
No new Merkle trees can ever be published and tree revocation is blocked.
Users can only claim from the old lastTree; new off-chain rewards cannot be distributed and the protocol becomes permanently non-functional.
resolveDispute() should successfully transfer the recorded disputeAmount back to the disputer or slash it to the governor, clearing the dispute.

recoverERC20() cannot help because resolveDispute() must succeed first to clear disputer, and depositing more tokens does not help since the FoT token takes fees on outgoing transfers; only upgrade/migration recovers.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether disputeTree() itself succeeds or reverts on the FoT deposit; only the received amount is described.
The exact FoT fee percentage is given only as an example (1%), not a fixed protocol parameter.
Report does not specify the concrete disputeAmount value beyond the illustrative 1000 tokens.
Whether the governor or disputer triggers resolveDispute() is not fixed; both branches are described.
